title: Orion Finance - customer escalation war-room notes (2026-03-25)
content:
Summary:
Orion Finance reported increased tail latency and errors from our hosted API starting 2026-03-24 21:00 UTC. Customer-facing impact: delayed trade confirmations, reported to their ops team as ~30-90s spikes and occasional 5xx. They opened an escalation (JIRA-ORION-412).

Meeting purpose:
- Rapid sync to triage, decide immediate mitigations, and assign owners for RCA + customer communications.
- Goal: stabilize customer traffic to acceptable SLA and agree on next steps for root cause and post-mortem.

Attendees:
- Maya Patel (Redwood Customer Success, owner)
- Jun Park (Redwood SRE)
- Priya Nair (Redwood Backend/Serving Runtime)
- Liam O'Connor (Redwood Network/Infra)
- Sam Reynolds (Orion SRE - customer contact)
- Alex Chen (Orion Product) - joined briefly

Timeline (observed):
- 2026-03-24 20:50 UTC: Orion reports intermittent 5xx and 30-90s latency on generation endpoint.
- 2026-03-24 21:05 UTC: On-call SRE paged; initial mitigation: scaled replica pool up + enabled conservative batching policy for their route.
- 2026-03-24 21:25 UTC: Errors reduced but tail latency still 20-40s on peak requests.
- 2026-03-24 22:00 UTC: Customer escalated due to business impact; requested war-room.

Immediate observations from logs/metrics (Priya/Jun):
- Sudden increase in sequence-length distribution for Orion requests between 21:00-21:30 (avg tokens per request jumped ~3x).
- KV cache hit rate for their route degraded (cache warming thrash), resulting in more cold-start compute work.
- One pod was OOM-killed intermittently (node-level mem pressure) around 21:10 - 21:18; autoscaler created replacement pods.
- Network p99 egress latency for the region spiked concurrently (Liam) but not sufficient alone to explain 90s spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Workload change at customer side (longer inputs) causing cache misses + heavier per-request compute -> queueing/backpressure -> tail latency.
2) A recent config rollout to the dedicated pool (2026-03-24 20:30) unintentionally changed batching thresholds causing suboptimal batch formation for this traffic pattern.
3) Node memory pressure (OOMs) reduced available capacity leading to request retries and higher latency.

Agreed immediate mitigations (owners + ETA):
- Temporarily pin Orion route to a smaller batch profile and stricter concurrency per replica to prioritize latency over throughput (Priya) - ETA 15m.
- Increase dedicated pool capacity for Orion traffic by +2 replicas (Jun/Liam) - ETA 10m and monitor.
- Disable recent batch-threshold rollout for the shard that hosts Orion (Priya) if latency persists - ETA 30m to rollback.
- Provide Orion with a short mitigation communication (Maya) - send update in 30m stating observed causes and actions.

Short-term checks (to run now):
- Verify current token length distribution for Orion (Sam/Jun) - confirm if customer-side prompt changes correlate.
- Inspect pod OOM logs and kernel messages for nodes that had evictions (Jun).
- Check autoscaler events and if any throttling or provisioning delays occurred (Liam).
- Confirm KV cache eviction rates and whether aggressive TTL or invalidation patterns are present (Priya).

Action items (owner | due):
- Priya: Apply stricter batch profile + monitor p50/p95/p99 latency on Orion route; revert recent threshold rollout if no improvement | due 2026-03-25 12:00 UTC.
- Jun: Add +2 replicas to Orion's dedicated pool and watch for OOMs/evictions; collect node mem metrics | due 2026-03-25 11:45 UTC.
- Liam: Validate network egress metrics for region, confirm no cloud provider incident; escalate to infra if necessary | due 2026-03-25 11:30 UTC.
- Maya: Draft and send interim update to Orion (what we saw, immediate mitigations, expected next update in 1 hour) and coordinate customer expectations | due 2026-03-25 11:15 UTC.
- Sam (Orion): Share any recent changes to prompt shapes, batching on client side, or traffic patterns since 2026-03-24 20:00 UTC | due 2026-03-25 11:00 UTC.
- Jun/Priya: Prepare data for RCA (query traces, token length histograms, cache metrics, pod OOM traces) and pull initial timeline for post-mortem | due 2026-03-26 18:00 UTC.

Customer comms plan:
- T+30m: Maya send interim note acknowledging escalation and listing immediate mitigations.
- T+2h: Technical update with metrics snapshot and whether rollback was required.
- T+24h: Post-mortem with root cause, corrective actions, and preventative measures.

Notes / decisions made in meeting:
- We will prioritize latency SLOs for Orion until we complete RCA.
- No customer-visible rollback of model versions; change is limited to batching/concurrency and capacity.
- If mitigations fail, plan B is to route Orion to a different hardware pool with higher memory and conservative batching (requires change window).

Outstanding questions:
- Did Orion change request sizes client-side (Sam)?
- Was there a correlated rollout across other customers around 20:30 that could indicate a platform regression?
- Are autoscaler thresholds too conservative for sudden token-burst traffic?

Follow-ups (next meeting schedule):
- 2026-03-25 12:00 UTC - 30m follow-up to review mitigations and decide on rollback or plan B. Invite: Maya, Jun, Priya, Liam, Sam.

Raw links / artifacts referenced:
- JIRA-ORION-412 (incident)
- Initial runbook draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/orion-incident-pr
- Confluence incident page: confluence://orion-incident-2026-03-25

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep comms short and frequent. Customer is jittery due to trading windows - be explicit about timelines.
- Add a paragraph to post-mortem template about prompt-shape-induced cache thrash to check impact on other customers.

End of notes.
